increment: resource-budget scope unification and full-process-tree measurement surface audit
method: static verification of budget scopes (thread_budget, resource-governor, Job Object cap, tool isolation) against live state/logs and the afece7e4/d4773c87 increments; gap matrix against the P8 measurement surface; no code or codex mutation

core_budget_cap.scope: application-level concurrency only: threads_per_worker × parallel_workers ≤ core_budget = min(5, logical_cores); a lower-only envelope; env setdefault for OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMEXPR; never an OS thread-count cap and never machine settings
core_budget_cap.gap: nothing aggregates the resulting live thread count of the process tree

soft_ledger.control_law: first over-budget sample engages regulation; ≥80% band pre-throttle; release after 5 consecutive under-80% samples (REGULATE_OVER_SAMPLES=1, REGULATE_UNDER_SAMPLES=5, factor 0.8)

hard_cap.mechanism: Windows Job Object CPU rate control, shared job ('worker-aggregate'), children inherit membership
hard_cap.default: OFF (resource-governor-rules.json features false; enabled only by --worker-job-cap / --worker-job-percent)
hard_cap.semantics: CpuRate = worker_job_percent × 100 (machine share); RAM has NO hard cap
hard_cap.known_defect: 708/1219 job assignments report ok=false (nesting refusal) and record.job_member is set unconditionally → failed assignments are never retried (resource-governor.py:911-924)

unit_unification.fix: afece7e4 normalized the per-process cpu_percent aggregate (per-core scale) to machine-% once before the over_budget comparison; ledger field and both verifiers share machine-%
unit_unification.effect: historical INT-10 over-budget flags were false positives; 0 true exceedances under the corrected unit (int-10-budget-unit-mismatch-20260922.json)

worker_plane_aggregate_cap.live_state_verification: main-system/runtime/state/resource-governor.json (2026-09-23T06:18Z) still shows pre-fix generation (worker_ledger.cpu_pct=11.6, over_budget=true, admission_hold=true, no worker_job_cap fields); state file must be regenerated by the running governor before any post-fix acceptance claim

scope_unification_finding: CORE_BUDGET_CAP=5 (Python pool thread budget, per-process) and the worker-plane aggregate hard cap (OS machine-share for worker/toolbox/repo-other) are different scopes and must not be reported as one number; the relation between the 5-core application budget and the 10% machine-share ledger requires a governor ruling; the Job hard cap remains opt-in
